*   # US Government Sold $728 Billion of Treasuries this Week. Yields at the 3-Year, 10-Year, 30-Year Auctions Highest in 20+ Years, Demand Emerges

    [From wolfstreet.com](https://wolfstreet.com/2026/10/10/us-government-sold-728-billion-of-treasuries-this-week-yields-at-the-3-year-10-year-30-year-auctions-highest-in-20-years-demand-emerges-short-term-yields-see-rate-hike/)

    [![](https://assets.faireconomy.media/nfs/npd/2021/01/13/npd_20_37_35.v2.png)](https://wolfstreet.com/2026/10/10/us-government-sold-728-billion-of-treasuries-this-week-yields-at-the-3-year-10-year-30-year-auctions-highest-in-20-years-demand-emerges-short-term-yields-see-rate-hike/)

    https://wolfstreet.com/2026/10/10/us-government-sold-728-billion-of-treasuries-this-week-yields-at-the-3-year-10-year-30-year-auctions-highest-in-20-years-demand-emerges-short-term-yields-see-rate-hike/

    The US government sold $728 billion of Treasury securities during the week, spread over eight auctions. Of them, $607 billion were Treasury bills with maturities from 4 weeks to 26 weeks, spread over six auctions. Four of these auctions were over $100 billion each. Most of these sales replaced maturing T-bills. The “investment rate” – which is the yield that is comparable to the yield of notes and bonds – on all of them was over 4%. And $121 billion of the auction sales were 3-year and 10-year Treasury notes and 30-year Treasury bonds. Yields at these three auctions blew through the yield ceiling in a big ...
